summary: Roosevelt announces he is willing to mediate between Russia and Japan. The Cabinet weighs a special session on tariff cuts, and he sees Beveridge, Platt and George Perkins. He writes Richard Harding Davis about good and bad ambassadors, the bad ones being 'pink tea men'.

events.detail: Cabinet on a special tariff session
Statement offering his services as peacemaker between Russia and Japan
Beveridge, Platt and Perkins at intervals; lunch with General Frazier

letters.topic: Good ambassadors and bad ones

tr_quotes.text: pink tea men

uncertain: Lunch with Frazier listed at 4:30 p.m.

headline: Climbing Rock Creek with the boys
summary: Congress returns. Roosevelt sees Pinchot, Garfield, Fairbanks and others. He tells Emlen Roosevelt and his wife of a recent clamber along Rock Creek with Ted, Kermit, Archie and Archie's friends, writes Taft about Army weapons, and refuses to carve land out of Yosemite National Park.

events.detail: Callers: Pinchot, Garfield, Hitchcock, Heyburn, Fairbanks
Letters to the Emlen Roosevelts, Taft and Needham

letters.topic: A scramble up Rock Creek with the boys
Army bayonets, swords and rifles
Won't let lands be cut from Yosemite

headline: Speaking to the American Forest Congress
summary: Roosevelt speaks to the American Forest Congress, meeting at the National Theatre. He talks freight rates with Senator Elkins, meets Senator Dick, and hosts a Cabinet dinner; illustrator Howard Pyle, the Whitridges and their wives stay the night.

events.detail: Address to the American Forest Congress
The Pyles and Whitridges stay overnight

works.title: Address to the American Forest Congress

headline: Arbitration treaties go to the Senate
summary: Seven general arbitration treaties, with Spain, Italy, Portugal, Switzerland, Germany, France and Britain, go to the Senate. Roosevelt hosts a dinner on Southern questions and complains to Spooner that senators want to curb presidential power by calling every agreement a treaty.

events.detail: Dinner on Southern issues with Jones, McBee, Abbott, Butler and Southern congressmen
Seven arbitration treaties submitted to the Senate

letters.topic: Senate's push to treat every agreement as a treaty
Fairbanks's Canadian report; their split over arbitration

uncertain: 'Judge Jones' taken as Thomas G. Jones of Alabama.

headline: Senate leaders on arbitration and tariff
summary: Roosevelt meets congressional leaders including Aldrich, Spooner, Cannon and Payne on the arbitration treaties, tariff bills and a possible special session. The Senate tacks a special-agreement amendment onto the treaties. He lunches with Munro Ferguson and dines with Dr. Lambert.

events.detail: Congressional leaders on treaties, tariff and an extra session

headline: Higgins and Stranahan to dinner
summary: Judge Thomas Jones calls at midday, and Roosevelt dines with New York's Governor Frank Higgins and Nevada Stranahan.

headline: A raise for Dr. Gorgas
summary: Roosevelt confers on railroad rates, naval appropriations and more, then attends a dinner given by Fairbanks. He tells Taft that canal sanitation chief Dr. Gorgas should be paid $10,000 a year, rebuffs Maria Storer's lobbying, and notes the Beef Trust case has reached the Supreme Court.

events.detail: Rail rates with Townsend and Esch
Fairbanks's dinner with Hemenway, Aldrich, Lodge and Allison
Letters to Taft, Maria Storer, Moody and Niedringhaus

letters.topic: Gorgas deserves $10,000 a year
Her renewed requests for favors and a Paris post for Bellamy
Beef Trust case now before the Supreme Court
Premature congratulations on a Missouri Senate seat

headline: No halt in building the Navy
summary: Roosevelt issues a statement calling for immediate tariff revision, holds a Cabinet meeting, and dines at John Hay's. He tells Representative George Foss he earnestly hopes naval building will not pause, and writes Sternberg about German policy in China.

events.detail: Letters to Foss, McCook, Cullom and Sternberg

letters.topic: Keep building up the Navy
Rail rates and legislation
The arbitration treaties
Germany's China policy

tr_quotes.text: I most earnestly hope that there will be no halt in the building up of the navy.

headline: Ratify the treaties as written
summary: Roosevelt publicly urges the Senate to ratify the arbitration treaties without amendment. He hosts a big dinner with Bob Ferguson, Justices Harlan and Brewer, Pinchot and others, drops in on the architects' dinner at the Arlington, and tells Lyman Abbott he treats the tariff as a matter of expediency.

events.detail: Statement for ratifying the arbitration treaties unamended
Palmer, Graves and Sheffield at lunch
Tariff views shared with Lyman Abbott

letters.topic: He will get what he can on the tariff

tr_quotes.text: on the tariff, which I regard as a matter of expediency, I shall endeavor to get the best results I can.

headline: Henry James at the White House
summary: Roosevelt's lunch table gathers Henry Adams, painter John La Farge, sculptor Augustus Saint-Gaudens and novelist Henry James, who stays the night after the diplomatic reception. Roosevelt also confers with Cullom on the treaties and writes Hay and Sternberg about China.

events.detail: Lunch with Straus, Shaffer, Hopkins, Garfield, Adams, La Farge, Saint-Gaudens and James
The Brocks and Henry James stay over
Letters to Hay, Sternberg and Leupp

letters.topic: A note from the Czar concerning China
China
The Newsboys Magazine and the Panama Canal

headline: Canal commission report to Congress
summary: The Isthmian Canal Commission's report goes to Congress. Roosevelt confers on the treaties, discusses making Joseph Bristow a special Panama Railroad commissioner, sees Owen Wister and goes to the National Theatre. He flatly refuses Representative Foss's idea of pausing naval building for a year.

events.detail: Treaties with Cullom, Grosvenor and Hopkins
Bristow's Panama Railroad assignment with Taft and Long
Canal commission report sent to Congress
Letters to Cannon, Foss and Hay

letters.topic: Appointments
Rejects a one-year halt in warship construction
Spring Rice is en route to America

headline: Talking railroads with James J. Hill
summary: Roosevelt goes over railroad rate changes with Hepburn and Taft and with Morton and railroad magnate James J. Hill. Oscar Straus and Jusserand are among his callers, and he writes Dr. William Sturgis Bigelow about a letter the Japanese envoy's son sent Archie.

events.detail: Rate revision with Taft and Hepburn

letters.topic: A letter to Archie from the son of Japan's envoy

headline: Treaty talk on Sunday night
summary: Roosevelt confers with Senators Daniel, Foster and McCreary about the arbitration pacts at nine, then sees W. W. Rockhill. Edith writes Emily that she liked Henry James, and that her husband changed his mind and liked him too.

events.detail: Arbitration treaties with McCreary, Foster and Daniel
Edith's letter to Emily about Henry James

headline: Saint-Gaudens for the coinage
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Costello, Nelson and Page. He directs Hay to write both Japan and Russia urging them not to violate China's neutrality, and tells Treasury Secretary Shaw he wants Augustus Saint-Gaudens to design new American coins.

events.detail: Page, Nelson and Costello at lunch

letters.topic: Ask Japan and Russia to respect Chinese neutrality
Have Saint-Gaudens design the coins

headline: Steamboat inspection and naval spending
summary: After a Cabinet meeting, Roosevelt discusses the steamboat inspection probe with George Uhler and naval appropriations with Morton and Taft. Treasury Secretary Shaw gives a dinner, and Roosevelt writes Robert Underwood Johnson about Yosemite and Yellowstone.

events.detail: Naval appropriations with Morton and Taft

letters.topic: Yosemite and Yellowstone national parks

headline: Bamie turns fifty
summary: On his sister Bamie's 50th birthday, Roosevelt goes over the Beef Trust investigation with Moody and Solomon Bethea. He tells Benjamin Ide Wheeler he wants a strong ICC and wires Sternberg that Britain, Italy, Germany and the U.S. stand behind China's territorial integrity.

events.detail: Beef Trust probe with Moody and Bethea
Letters to Wheeler and Moody; telegram to Sternberg

letters.topic: Favors a powerful ICC
The Hepburn rate bill
Telegram: four powers guarantee China's integrity

headline: Diplomatic dinner and a houseful of girls
summary: Roosevelt confers with Knox and hosts a diplomatic dinner at the White House. Three young guests, Eleanor Whitridge, Isabella Selmes and Lorraine Roosevelt, stay the night.

headline: Old friends from the West
summary: Roosevelt confers with Representative Dayton on naval spending and lunches with Bishop William Lawrence and a crowd that includes his old ranch partner Frank Merrifield, Pinchot, Leupp, Philip Stewart and the Swiss Minister. He dines with J. S. Elliott.

events.detail: Large lunch with Bishop Lawrence, Merrifield, Pinchot and others

uncertain: 'F. W. Merrifield' assumed to be Badlands partner Bill (A. W.) Merrifield, a Montana elector per Jan. 23.

headline: A new room for Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt receives William Jennings Bryan and lunches with Charles Emory Smith. He hires architect Grant La Farge to add a large north room to Sagamore Hill for $16,000, nearly what the whole house cost in 1884, with work to run from March to June.

events.detail: Contracts with La Farge for the North Room

uncertain: 'Hull' taken as Rep. John A. T. Hull.

headline: Sunday supper
summary: Roosevelt has supper with J. S. Elliott.

headline: Boxing with a wrestler
summary: Roosevelt writes Kermit about presidential electors in town, among them Frank Merrifield from Montana. He and Ted keep boxing with Grant, a wrestler and so-so boxer; young Corinne and her friends visited for the diplomats' dinner; Archie and Quentin have the grippe; and he has finished reading The Deerslayer to them.

events.detail: Boxing sessions with Ted and the wrestler Grant
Archie and Quentin down with the grippe

letters.topic: Electors, boxing with Grant, the girls' visit, sick boys, Cooper

tr_quotes.text: Ted and I continue to box with Grant, the wrestler. He isn't a very good boxer for a prizefighter
Little Corinne, with Isabella Selmes, Lorraine and two other girls have been here for the Diplomatic Dinner
Archie and Quentin had the grip [sic], and Quentin is still in bed. I have finished reading The Deerslayer to them.

uncertain: 'Little Corinne' taken as niece Corinne Douglas Robinson; '[sic]' is the compiler's.

headline: Wichita game preserve created
summary: A new law creates the Wichita Game Preserve. Roosevelt attends a Peabody trustees' meeting at the Arlington Hotel, lunches with Shaw, Governor Francis and Saint-Gaudens, receives the Japanese and British envoys, and he and Edith dine with the Tafts.

events.detail: Lunch with Shaw, David Francis and Saint-Gaudens
Receives the ministers of Japan and Britain
Taft gives a dinner for the Roosevelts

uncertain: The envoys are not named in source; Takahira and Durand identified tentatively.

headline: Corporate law in the capital
summary: Roosevelt confers with Speaker Cannon and lunches with Bamie, Perkins, Berry and Hasbrouck. He tells Moody that the District of Columbia's laws governing corporations fall short.

events.detail: Letter to Moody on D.C. corporation law

letters.topic: Weak rules on corporations in the District

uncertain: 'Parkins' may be George W. Perkins; Hasbrouck taken as Gilbert Hasbrouck.

headline: Pressing the Roosevelt Corollary
summary: Roosevelt attends Mrs. Warren's wedding at noon, addresses a church conference on marriage and divorce, and hosts the judiciary dinner. He tells Elbert Baldwin he wants authority to act on his Caribbean policy and writes Hay about running Santo Domingo's customshouses.

events.detail: Speech to an interchurch gathering on marriage and divorce

letters.topic: Seeks power to apply his corollary; the Santo Domingo treaty
Dillingham-Sanchez protocol; Dominican territory if the U.S. runs customs

works.title: Address to the Interchurch Conference on Marriage and Divorce

uncertain: Mrs. Bishop's first name supplied.

headline: Cutting corners on the North Room?
summary: After the Cabinet meeting Roosevelt sees Senators Aldrich, Bard and Dietrich and Representative Crumpacker, and lunches with Joe Bishop. He asks Grant La Farge whether Sagamore Hill's new North Room could be built for less by using cheaper woods.

events.detail: Aldrich, Bard, Dietrich and Crumpacker call
Letter to La Farge on costs

letters.topic: Savings on wood and materials for the North Room

headline: Sketched by Ellen Day Hale
summary: Artist Ellen Day Hale sketches Roosevelt at nine in the morning. A packed day follows: treaty and Alaska talks, lunch with journalist Ray Stannard Baker, calls from Booker T. Washington and Bishop Satterlee, and the Gridiron Club dinner. He vents to Lyman Abbott about the stalled treaties.

events.detail: Ellen Day Hale draws his portrait
Two letters to Hay; one to Abbott

letters.topic: Newfoundland and Santo Domingo treaties; Korea (two letters)
Frustration over the stalled arbitration treaties

headline: Spring Rice's secret visit
summary: Cecil Spring Rice arrives quietly in Washington, sent by the British government to talk with Roosevelt, who does not get on with Ambassador Durand. Staying with Henry Adams and dining with the President, he warns of Russia's sweeping Asian ambitions and harsh crackdown at home. The press never learns of the visit.

events.detail: Spring Rice arrives on a confidential mission
Briefing on Russian aims and repression

uncertain: Source adds that Spring Rice later sent such intelligence in letters addressed to Edith.

headline: Annapolis graduation and a Philadelphia speech
summary: Roosevelt addresses the graduating class at the Naval Academy in Annapolis, then speaks that evening at a Union League Club banquet in Philadelphia, calling for a stronger Interstate Commerce Commission able to enforce fair railroad rates. He also sends Congress a message about corporations operating in the capital.

events.detail: Union League Club dinner address on rail regulation
Message to Congress on D.C. corporations

works.title: Address at the U.S. Naval Academy
Address to the Union League Club of Philadelphia
Message on corporations in the District of Columbia

uncertain: Source prints the Annapolis time as '41:00 a.m.'; read as 11:00.

headline: Taking over Dominican customs
summary: Roosevelt urges the Senate to ratify the arbitration treaties at once. The Beef Trust ruling is affirmed by the Supreme Court, and over congressional objections the U.S., at the Dominican government's invitation, takes charge of its customshouses. That evening he and Edith dine with Attorney General Moody.

events.detail: Statement for quick ratification of the arbitration treaties
Supreme Court affirms the Beef Trust decision
U.S. assumes control of Dominican customshouses

letters.topic: Harriman blocks a railroad man's appointment in Arizona
